content.title: About
content.content: Pre-gelatinized chickpea flour is made from dried chickpeas that undergo partial hydrolysis and drying. This process makes the flour readily soluble in cold liquids and improves its gelling ability. It is widely used in gluten‑free cooking, sauces, soups, and baked goods.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chickpea flour is a rich source of plant protein and dietary fiber.
The pre‑gelatinized form thickens cold beverages without heating.
Chickpeas (Cicer arietinum) are cultivated in the Mediterranean, South Asia, and North Africa.
Traditional Indian cuisine uses chickpea flour for pakoras, bhajis, and chutneys.
Pre‑gelatinized flour has a longer shelf life than regular flour due to lower moisture activity.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Chickpea flour provides about 20 % protein, supporting muscle maintenance and satiety.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and helps maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: The flour raises blood glucose slowly, making it suitable for diabetics.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Safe for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to chickpeas.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption; soaking or fermenting can mitigate this.

items.title: Carbohydrate load
items.content: While the glycemic index is low, the total carbohydrate amount can be high in large servings.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add the flour to bread, pancake, or cake batters, or use it as a thickener for sauces, soups, and smoothies. The pre‑gelatinized version can be mixed directly with cold water or milk without heating.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For extended storage, refrigerate or freeze to preserve freshness.
